decisions.reason: Strong adoption by the UK Home Office and connections to over 30 government APIS schemes largely resolves uncertainty about its value, so the option is retained.
The travel health requirements API shows no adoption and demand has likely faded as pandemic-related requirements are removed, so its option value is unlikely to be realized.
Cyber security awareness training leverages existing training resources and is relatively inexpensive to keep while demand grows, making it a valuable option.
The behaviour analysis security system has only a brief mention and no evidence of adoption, suggesting high cost and unresolved value that do not justify continued commitment.
Passenger security profiling has low visibility and faces likely regulatory and ethical hurdles, so the option is unlikely to realize value and is abandoned.

The dedicated web platform page indicates some commitment, but without results, uncertainty remains high and the option is kept open at low cost while travel and document verification demand may develop.
